title: How John Rush runs a portfolio of bootstrapped startups with AI, a shared audience and co-makers
summary: John Rush explains how he validates many startup ideas by pitching them to a large audience he built on LinkedIn, X and Reddit, then building only the ones that draw engagement. Because the same audience uses multiple products, he treats lifetime value as the sum across his whole portfolio.

principles.text: Build a distribution channel first, pitch many ideas, and only build the ones that draw engagement.
principles.quote: I built this massive distribution channel on LinkedIn X and other and Reddit and then I pitch my ideas a lot of ideas and whenever I see one idea that gets a lot of comments and likes and questions from the users I take it forward

principles.text: A shared audience across many products multiplies lifetime value, since LTV sums across all products one person uses.
principles.quote: lifetime value now is a sum of all my products that are used by the same person in average. So if otherwise lifetime value of one product is $400 for example but if I have 10 products then it's $4,000.
